title: Minimap opens on the alphabetically-first scope, hiding freshly explored cells

sections.what: `render()` in `static/js/agent/turn-minimap.ts` builds the scope `<select>` from `payload.scopes` in server order and never assigns an initial `sel.value`, so the panel opens on the first `<option>`. The server sorts scopes by scope id (`routes/player_ops.py:1607`, `sorted(scope_counts.items())`), so the default is the alphabetically-first scope id, not the scope that holds `payload.current_area`. `paint()` then filters the visited areas to the selected scope, so any cell explored in another scope is not drawn.
sections.why: Measured live 2026-10-17 against scenario `kraktooth_goblin_camp`. Cullen Rutherford stands in `Road (world 13,7)` (scope `world`), with 3 visited cells in `world` and 1 in `goblin_camp`. The panel opens on `goblin camp (1)` and draws one cell. To the player this reads as the minimap having lost where they went: they moved N/W/S, saw the cells (they had switched the dropdown), ran a timeskip, reopened the human turn composer, and only the cells in the default scope were left. Every open re-renders a fresh select with no persisted choice, so the selection silently resets to the first scope. The map payload itself is byte-stable across the timeskip (same areas, same scopes), so no observation is lost - the panel is simply looking at the wrong scope. Caveat: this explanation only covers cells the character gained in a scope other than the first. If the cells that disappeared were all inside the first scope, then the panel is telling the truth and the loss is real; that case points at observation or serialization loss instead, and needs its own repro (capture `/api/players/<name>/map` before and after the timeskip and diff the `areas` and `scopes`).
sections.how: In `turn-minimap.ts render()`, after the options are appended, set `sel.value` to the scope id of the current area: find the entry in `payload.areas` whose `name === payload.current_area`, read its `scope_id`, and select it when it matches an option; otherwise keep the fallback to the first option. Apply the same default in `openFullscreen()`. Both `current_area` and `areas[].scope_id` are already in the `/api/players/<name>/map` payload (`routes/player_ops.py handle_get_player_map`), so no server change is needed. Edit the `.ts` and rebuild; do not hand-edit the emitted `.js`.
sections.verify:
1. Start the app (`python app.py`, port 4444), load `kraktooth_goblin_camp`, and give a human character cells in two scopes.
   - expected: the map scope dropdown shows the current area's scope selected and draws that scope's cells.
   - observed: 2026-10-23, real browser against `http://127.0.0.1:4455` (isolated server) with a payload whose `scopes` are the server-sorted `goblin_camp` then `world` and whose current area `Road` is in `world`. `TurnMinimap.render(host, payload)` set the inline `<select>` to `world`, not the first option `goblin_camp`. The fullscreen `<select>` also opened on `world`.
2. Switch the dropdown, then close and reopen the panel.
   - expected: it opens on the current area's scope again, showing all cells there.
   - observed: a fresh `render()` with the same payload re-selected `world`; the scope list and the `change` handler are unchanged, so switching still repaints. Two fallback cases were also measured: `current_area` that matches no area name but carries `current: true` selected `world`, and a payload with no `current` marker selected the first scope `goblin_camp`.
3. `python tools/ts_convert.py check` after the `.ts` edit.
   - expected: pass
   - observed: did not pass globally on 2026-10-23. The failures are outside this file: `static/js/inspector/agent-view.ts(2869,1): error TS1005: '}' expected` (another lane's dirty file), eslint `action-verbs.generated.js` `'module' is not defined`, a missing `@module` contract on `static/js/ui/source-version.js`, the pre-existing `test_plan_grounding.js` failure, and an unreviewed `window.` drop in `static/js/main.js`. `npx eslint static/js/agent/turn-minimap.js` passed, and a scoped `tsc` (`extends ./tsconfig.json`, include only `turn-minimap.ts`) emitted the `.js` with exit 0.

acceptance.text: The minimap panel opens on the scope of `payload.current_area` when that scope is present, and falls back to the first scope only when it is not.
Switching scope still redraws; the fullscreen map uses the same default.
No `.js` under `static/js/` is hand-edited; the emitted file was produced by `tsc` from the `.ts`. The global `ts_convert.py check` is blocked by unrelated files, named above.

custom.browser_ui: Intended UI home: the human turn composer (HTC) scene column, the `Where you've been` panel and its fullscreen map. Current availability: the panel works and draws, but opens on the wrong scope. Live path: load a scenario where the active character has visited cells in two scopes, open their turn, and confirm the scope dropdown opens on the scope of the current area and draws every cell visited there. Switch scope and confirm the other cells draw; close and reopen the panel and confirm it opens on the current scope again.
custom.verified_2026_10_23_live:
Measured in the real browser on an isolated server (port 4455) by calling the
emitted `TurnMinimap.render` with a controlled payload. The assertion is the
`<select>.value`, not the source text:

| Case | Scopes order | Current area | Selected |
|---|---|---|---|
| current area in a non-first scope | `goblin_camp`, `world` | `Road` (scope `world`) | `world` |
| fullscreen, same payload | `goblin_camp`, `world` | `Road` (scope `world`) | `world` |
| name mismatch, server marker `current: true` | `goblin_camp`, `world` | unknown name | `world` |
| no current marker | `goblin_camp`, `world` | none | `goblin_camp` |

The last row is the old behaviour kept as the documented fallback.
custom.reconciliation_2026_10_20_still_valid_re:
**Verdict: STILL_VALID.** task-882 rewrote this file but did not fix the default-scope defect; the card's premise still holds.

**Re-measured 2026-10-20.**
- `render()` in `static/js/agent/turn-minimap.ts:561-641` still builds the scope `<select>` from `payload.scopes` in server order and never assigns an initial `sel.value`; it falls through to `paint()` at line 640, which reads `sel.value` (the first `<option>`). Confirmed by reading the current source.
- `openFullscreen()` at lines 644-703 has the same gap: its own `<select>` is appended at line 657-664 with no default assignment before `paint()` at line 702.
- `routes/player_ops.py:1612` still sorts scopes with `for scope_id, count in sorted(scope_counts.items())`, so the default remains the alphabetically-first scope id, not the scope of `payload.current_area`.

**Newer work checked.** Commit `2821c9d8` (task-882, 2026-10-19) touched `static/js/agent/turn-minimap.ts` heavily (170 insertions) - it added sight-aware visible/charted cells, horizon landmarks, recall route queries and walk-to-area - but a `git show 2821c9d8 -- static/js/agent/turn-minimap.ts` grep for `sel.value` finds no assignment, and `git log --oneline -S "sel.value" -- static/js/agent/turn-minimap.ts` returns only `0b1d64df` (the original minimap commit). So the default-scope behaviour is untouched by task-882.

**Counts.** `grep -c "sel.value" static/js/agent/turn-minimap.ts` → 4 hits, all reads inside `paint()` (lines 624, 674) and the fullscreen paint (lines 675, 676); zero writes. That is the evidence the panel opens on the first scope.

**Cited line drift.** The card's `How` cites `render()` and `openFullscreen()` without line numbers; the current locations are `turn-minimap.ts:561` and `:644`. The `routes/player_ops.py:1607` reference in the What section has drifted to `:1612` (the `sorted(scope_counts.items())` call); corrected in place above. `handle_get_player_map` is now at `player_ops.py:1545` (was not cited by line). `payload.current_area` and `areas[].scope_id` are still both present in the payload (`player_ops.py:1562`, `:1600`), so the card's proposed fix needs no server change - confirming the card is still actionable as written.

**Status:** left in `todo`. The fix is a ~4-line addition in `render()` and `openFullscreen()` after the options are appended.
